35464172_230910bb.text: The LHA contains both glutamatergic and GABAergic neurons, although these classical neurotransmitters do not fully explain the roles of LHA in feeding and metabolic regulation (Stuber et al., 2016). The discovery of the sub-populations of neurons expressing distinct neuropeptides within the LHA considerably advances our understanding of the roles of LHA. These sub-populations of LHA neurons mainly include hypocretin/orexin-expressing neurons and melanin concentrating hormone (MCH)-releasing neurons (Bonnavion et al., 2016)

35464172_c17b37dc.text: .Functionally, the orexin, also known as hypocretin, is a neuropeptide that regulates arousal, sleep, appetite and motivated behavior (Tsujino et al., 2013). In addition, intracisternal injection of orexin antibody reduces food intake, suggesting that orexin regulates feeding [32]. Leptin treatment inhibits orexin expression and neuronal activity, while silencing of leptin signals increases orexin expression and elevates the excitatory synaptic inputs onto orexin neurons (Goforth et al., 2014). Leptin reduces orexin synthesis and secretion through LepR in LHA neurons or through the dopaminergic projection from the ventral tegmental area (VTA) to LHA to suppress food intake (Goforth et al., 2014)(Zheng et al., 2007). Surprisingly, orexin overexpression prevents diet-induced obesity through improving leptin sensitivity and enhancing energy expenditure (Funato et al., 2009). Overall, leptin control of orexin neurons is complex but required for appropriate energy balance.
